title: Jenna Elfman Joins a Spy Show Where Stephen Fry Unlocks Criminals' Minds!
summary:
Get ready for a new TV show that mixes spies, brain games, and a very odd partnership! Jenna Elfman, who you might know from the funny sitcom 'Dharma & Greg,' has just signed on to star in a Fox series called 'The Interrogator.' She'll be acting alongside Stephen Fry, who plays the main character, Conrad Henry. 

Conrad isn't your typical tough-guy spy. He's an MI6 agent (that's like the British version of the CIA) with a superpower: his brain. When regular questioning fails, Conrad uses his charm, smarts, and clever mind tricks to unlock the secrets of dangerous criminals. It's like he can pick the locks of their thoughts! 

Jenna Elfman will play a character named Woodrow. She used to be a rising star in the CIA, but a mission that went wrong knocked her down the career ladder. Now she's stuck as a handler for Conrad's team—basically, she has to keep an eye on him and make sure he doesn't go too far. She thinks it's a demotion, but she's determined to climb back up. The problem? Conrad is always seven steps ahead, and Woodrow is usually only five steps ahead. They argue a lot, but deep down, they respect each other. The show calls them "strange bedfellows," which means two people who don't seem like they'd get along but have to work together anyway. 

This is a big return to TV for Elfman. She became famous on 'Dharma & Greg,' where she won a Golden Globe and got three Emmy nominations. Since then, she's been in shows like 'Fear the Walking Dead' and 'Dark Winds.' Now she's diving into a world of espionage and mind games. 

The show was created by Stephen Fry himself, and it already has a full season of 12 episodes ordered. With a cast that also includes Luke Kleintank and Michael Beach, 'The Interrogator' promises to be a smart, twisty ride. Keep an eye out for it—it might just be your next favorite show!
why_it_matters: This show lets you imagine how brain power can be just as important as physical action in solving crimes, and it shows that odd-couple partners can be stronger together.

background_read: Jenna Elfman became famous in the late 1990s for her role in the comedy 'Dharma & Greg,' for which she won a Golden Globe Award.
Stephen Fry is a beloved British actor, comedian, and writer, known for hosting the quiz show QI and for roles in movies like 'V for Vendetta' and 'The Hobbit.'
Spy shows have been popular for decades; the British MI6 and the American CIA are real-world intelligence agencies that inspire many fictional stories.
Article_Structure: WHO: Jenna Elfman, actress known for 'Dharma & Greg,' and Stephen Fry, who created and stars in the series.
WHAT: A spy show called 'The Interrogator' about an MI6 agent with a talent for psychological interrogation, and his handler, a demoted CIA officer.
WHERE: On the Fox television network, with a full season of 12 episodes ordered.
WHY: The show mixes espionage, clever mind games, and a tense but respectful partnership between two very different spies.

perspectives.description: The mental duels and spy tricks make it a thinking person's thriller, where outsmarting the bad guy is more exciting than car chases.
After years away from a regular TV role, seeing her play a tough, clever CIA officer is a treat for anyone who loved her comedic and dramatic work.
Some might think mind-reading abilities are unrealistic, but the show promises to make the psychological tricks feel clever and believable.
